title: Directed interval enclosure certifies the fixed rounded residual snapshot
question: Can directed interval arithmetic certify the residual minimum eigenvalue and both fixed-reference separations for the exact IEEE-754 rounded R-428/R-429 graph snapshot at the R-426 failure row?
method: Reconstruct the fixed R-426 row through the hash-pinned R-429 snapshot producer without importing the R-431 primary result.

Represent every binary64 weight and conductance as its exact binary rational and propagate 80-digit directed mpmath intervals through the symmetric conductance hull, weighted residual basis and compression.
Certify the lower eigenvalue bound by interval Cholesky positivity of A-LI at L=5.3631875357, and certify the upper bound with an interval Rayleigh quotient below 5.3631875359.
Repeat the construction independently with reversed block and anchor order and reversed Cholesky pivot order; retain the unchanged 5e-7 R-426 comparison tolerance.
Run hostile source/row/tolerance/status/promotion mutations and a Lean rational-threshold cross-check while keeping the original Hamiltonian source explicitly outside scope.
finding: The primary interval lane passes 16/16 assertions. The exact binary64 rounded snapshot has a certified residual bracket [5.3631875357, 5.3631875357858094719615598072499099181814069649417...], with matrix interval width below 1e-50. The lower endpoint exceeds the R-422 reference by 0.000002568536301..., and the upper endpoint lies below the R-426 direct reference by 0.0000008142620005..., so both one-sided separations exceed the fixed 5e-7 tolerance. The independent reversed-order lane passes 12/12 with upper endpoint 5.363187535785720770809451305696661..., the hostile lane rejects 7/7 mutations, the integrated verifier passes 15/15, and Lean R431 compiles.
decision_reason: A finite directed interval certificate removes downstream eigensolver and basis-rounding ambiguity for the exact R-429 binary64 graph snapshot. It does not enclose the upstream 256-dimensional Hamiltonian, coordinate eigenbasis or Gibbs normalization, so the original-source precision boundary and R-426 route status remain separate.
decision_scope: One finite V=2, cutoff d=16, beta=8, right-orientation conditional row 7, core/tail 7/9; exact binary64 rounded graph snapshot; no original-source interval, uniform limit or physical promotion.
boundary: This is a T0 claim-nonbearing finite interval certificate for a rounded snapshot. It does not certify the original rational Hamiltonian source, close residual reuse for the unrounded model, establish a cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion-uniform bound, or imply C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang--Mills or a mass gap.
next_action: Construct validated interval or ball enclosures for the original coordinate and Hamiltonian eigensystems, propagate them through Gibbs normalization and residual compression, and repeat the same fixed-row comparisons.

adversarial_review.check: Every stored binary64 value is treated as its exact binary rational; no decimal truncation or unrecorded source substitution is used.
Both conductance directions are enclosed by a symmetric interval hull before the residual operator is formed.
The lower probe is accepted only when every interval Cholesky pivot has a positive lower endpoint; a higher probe is rejected.
The upper endpoint comes from an interval Rayleigh quotient and is not inferred from the rejected Cholesky probe.
The 5e-7 tolerance and fixed row are read from the manifest and hostile mutations attempting relaxation are rejected.
The interval certificate is explicitly rounded-snapshot-only; original-source certification and residual-reuse closure remain false.
No cutoff/volume limit, common core, OS/KMS/GNS, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang--Mills or mass-gap statement is inferred.

no_overclaim: R-431 certifies only a finite residual eigenvalue bracket and two fixed-reference separations for the exact rounded graph snapshot. It does not certify the unrounded Hamiltonian source or any physical or continuum conclusion.
